name: WideSht's wave's spawn word
why: BN6's WideSht family (0x30) hands its wave's spawner r3 = 0x100000 where BN5's (0x25) hands 0, and the common spawn keeps the caller's r1-r4 as the object's words (r3 at +0x3C): the wave's +0x3E reads 0x10 in BN6's battle alone. No code of the wave's reads its +0x3C (its routines, BN5 0x080CC878 / BN6 0x080CCD0C, walked), and the battle goes on the same.
evidence: BN5 0x080ED132: movs r3,#0, then bl 0x080CCA62 (the wave's spawner); BN6 0x080EE93C-0x080EE93E: movs r3,#0x10; lsls r3,r3,#0x10, then bl 0x080CCEF6
the common spawn BN6 0x080032BC-0x080032C6: ldm r7!,{r0-r4} (the caller's r0-r4, pushed by its spawner); strb r0,[r5,#1]; str r1,[r5,#0x34]; str r2,[r5,#0x38]; str r3,[r5,#0x3c]; str r4,[r5,#4]
chip_widesht1-3: the wave's +0x3E 0 in BN5's and 0x10 in BN6's from its spawn, every other byte of it the same
